passage:
At lunch break, Harsha opened his steel tiffin. Beside him, Omkar was staring at the window with nothing on his desk.
"Where's your tiffin?" Harsha whispered.
"Forgot it. It's okay."
"You're not eating anything?"
"I'll drink water."
Harsha looked at his lemon rice. Mum always packed a lot. "Here," he said, pushing the lid across. "Take half."
"Really? It's yours."
"There's too much. Just take it. Use my spoon, I have another."
Omkar hesitated, then scooped some rice onto the lid. "Thanks, Harsha. This is really good."
"Mum puts peanuts in it."
Harsha ate his half slowly. His stomach felt a little empty, but warm all the same. When Omkar laughed at a joke at the back of the class, Harsha smiled to himself.

qa.q: What food did Harsha share with Omkar?
qa.a: Harsha shared half of his lemon rice.

qa.q: How did Harsha feel after giving half of his lunch?
qa.a: He felt warm and content, even though his stomach was a little empty. He smiled to himself when Omkar laughed.

qa.q: What could Omkar do to keep the friendship fair if a lunch is ever forgotten again?
qa.a: Omkar could say thank you again, and another day bring something to share with Harsha, so giving goes both ways. 😊

qa.q: How might Omkar have felt when Omkar said it was okay and would just drink water?
qa.a: Omkar may have felt embarrassed or shy about not having food, and not wanting to be a bother. Harsha's easy offer let Omkar accept without feeling small.

grounding: A child gives half his tiffin to a hungry classmate without being told and feels warm afterwards.

passage:
At recess I noticed Amandeep sitting alone on the steps by the bus lane. Everyone else was eating. His hands were in his lap, and he was watching the ants.
I had two parathas that day. Nobody had told me to do anything. I just thought that my stomach was full and his wasn't. So I walked over and tore one paratha in half. "Want this?" I said.
He looked surprised. "You sure?" I nodded. He ate it fast, then said thanks in a small voice.
I didn't tell anyone. Afterwards I felt light, like when you run and stop. I started looking for who else was sitting alone. I'm Rafiq, and that was the first time I noticed that I liked giving.

qa.q: What did Rafiq give to Amandeep?
qa.a: Rafiq tore one of his two parathas in half and gave it to Amandeep.

qa.q: How did Rafiq feel after giving away half a paratha?
qa.a: Rafiq felt light and glad, like after running and stopping, and began noticing who else was sitting alone.

qa.q: What could Rafiq do next if he wants to keep helping Amandeep without making him feel embarrassed?
qa.a: Rafiq could sit with Amandeep and share casually, as before. Asking Amandeep to play afterwards would help him feel included, not pitied.

qa.q: What was it like for Amandeep when Rafiq walked over?
qa.a: He was probably surprised and hungry, and maybe a little shy. He asked "You sure?" and ate quickly, which shows the food mattered to him.

grounding: A child gives half a lunch to a hungry classmate unprompted and feels warm afterwards, starting to see the narrator as someone who gives.
